chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the boy: when does salat (prayer) become obligatory upon him? He said: When he reaches thirteen years of age. But if he experiences iḥtilām before that, then salat (prayer) has become obligatory upon him and the pen has begun to run upon him. And the girl is like that: if she reaches thirteen years of age, or menstruates before that, then salat (prayer) has become obligatory upon her and the pen has begun to run upon her.

key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: experienced a wet dream; a sign of puberty for a boy
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: the girl; a female child to whom the parallel ruling applies
key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: the boy; a male child who is the subject of the ruling
key_terms.الْقَلَمُ: the pen; a metaphor for the beginning of legal accountability and recorded responsibility
key_terms.حَاضَتْ: menstruated; a sign of puberty for a girl

ai.seo_question: When does salat (prayer) become obligatory for a boy or girl in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the point at which salat (prayer) becomes obligatory for boys and girls, linking legal responsibility to age and to signs of puberty. It establishes that religious accountability begins upon reaching thirteen years or earlier physical maturity, and applies this ruling to both males and females.
